content: Largest Pharma Companies in the World (2026 Revenue Rankings) Get link Facebook X Pinterest Email Other Apps By Editorial Team - October 22, 2026 By the One Day Advisor Editorial Team | Reviewed by Frank Yap, MBA | Originally published June 2025 | Updated October 2026 (Q3 2026 results through Roche’s October 22 sales release) Quick Answer: What are the largest pharma companies in the world? Johnson & Johnson is the world’s largest pharmaceutical/healthcare company by revenue ($94.2 billion in 2025), followed by China’s distributor Sinopharm Group (~$80 billion), Roche (~$70 billion), Eli Lilly ($65.2 billion, +45%), Merck & Co. ($65.0 billion), Pfizer ($62.6 billion), AbbVie ($61.2 billion), AstraZeneca ($58.7 billion), Novartis ($54.5 billion) and Bristol Myers Squibb ($48.2 billion). Lilly is the largest by market capitalization (~$1.1 trillion). J&J raised 2026 guidance to ~$101.2 billion on October 13. What changed in this October 22, 2026 update New: Q3 2026 results from Johnson & Johnson (Oct 13) and Roche (Oct 22), plus a Q3 reporting calendar for the rest of the top 10. Fixed: conflicting 2026 guidance figures for J&J, Lilly, Merck and Pfizer now match the latest company guidance throughout the page. Added: a “Latest 2026 signal” column in the leaderboard, a pure-pharma vs. total-revenue explainer and an expanded FAQ. Unchanged by design: the ranking itself is based on closed FY2025 books; market caps remain early-August 2026 snapshots. Disclosure: This article is educational and is not financial, investment or medical advice. It contains TradingView links that may earn the site a commission at no cost to you. See the full disclaimer at the end. In this guide 2026 Top 20 Pharma Revenue & Market Cap Leaderboard Q3 2026 Update: J&J, Roche and What Reports Next Q2 2026 Earnings Roundup Pharma Revenue vs. Total Company Revenue Company-by-Company Breakdown (1–20) Key 2026 Growth Drivers Frequently Asked Questions Use This Ranking With Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini & Perplexity Methodology Read More & References The largest pharma companies in the world shape global healthcare through blockbuster drugs in cancer, cardiovascular disease, immunology, vaccines and metabolic disorders. They are defined not only by revenue but by scale, research investment and therapeutic reach. They typically: Spend tens of billions of dollars a year on R&D Operate across the U.S., Europe and emerging markets Control multiple blockbuster drug franchises Influence global drug pricing and treatment standards Boosted by a 45% jump in 2025 sales, Eli Lilly is now the fourth-largest company in the ranking, up from $45 billion in 2024 to $65.2 billion, according to its Q4 2025 results . The 2025 sales race at the top was tight: only about $170 million separated Lilly from Merck & Co., per Drug Discovery Trends’ Pharma 50 . Note: The global healthcare industry is much larger than Big Pharma. See Largest Healthcare Companies by Country (2026). Q3 2026 Update: J&J, Roche and What Reports Next Third-quarter earnings season is only just under way, so the FY2025 ranking above is unchanged. Two of the top three companies have now reported: Johnson & Johnson (Oct 13): Q3 sales rose 5.9% to $25.4 billion and Innovative Medicine grew 7.7% to $16.76 billion, led by oncology (Darzalex, Carvykti, Tecvayli, Rybrevant/Lazcluze, Erleada) plus Tremfya, Spravato and Caplyta. Adjusted EPS was $2.59, but GAAP EPS fell to $0.09 on roughly $7 billion in charges tied to a proposed talc litigation resolution, the Firefly Bio acquisition and the Sail Biomedicines collaboration. J&J raised 2026 reported-sales guidance to $101.0–101.4 billion (midpoint $101.2 billion) and adjusted EPS guidance to $11.05–$11.15. Details: J&J press release . Roche (Oct 22): Nine-month group sales reached CHF 46.5 billion, up 6% at constant exchange rates but only 1% in Swiss francs because of the strong franc. Q3 alone grew 7% at CER (8% in CHF). Pharmaceuticals rose 7% CER to CHF 36.2 billion; Diagnostics rose 4% CER to CHF 10.3 billion. The 2026 outlook (mid-single-digit sales growth, high-single-digit core EPS growth) was confirmed. Details: Roche release . Q3 2026 reporting calendar (remaining top-10 names) Company Q3 2026 report Watch for Eli Lilly Late October (company-confirmed date; verify on Lilly IR ) Foundayo launch, tirzepatide pricing, raise to the $85–87B guide AbbVie Oct 30, per published calendars Skyrizi/Rinvoq vs. Humira erosion Pfizer Nov 3, per Barchart via inkl ; consensus EPS ~$0.72 Non-COVID growth, cost-savings progress Novo Nordisk Nov 4 ( company calendar ) Second guidance raise, oral Wegovy uptake Merck, Novartis, AstraZeneca, BMS Late Oct–early Nov (confirm on each IR page) Keytruda mix, Novartis generic erosion, Q3 guidance changes Q2 2026 Earnings Roundup Calendar-Q2 2026 results (late July to early August) were broadly strong: six of the top ten companies by revenue raised full-year guidance. Johnson & Johnson: Q2 revenue +6.6% to $25.31 billion; Innovative Medicine +7.8% to $16.38 billion (Tremfya +72.5% to $2 billion). Eli Lilly: Q2 revenue +47.7% to $22.97 billion; adjusted EPS $8.38, about 27% above consensus; 2026 guidance raised to $85–87 billion. Merck & Co.: Q2 revenue +5% to $16.6 billion; newly launched products more than doubled to $1.5 billion; guidance raised to $66.3–67.3 billion despite a $2.31-per-share charge tied to its Terns Pharmaceuticals acquisition. Pfizer: Q2 revenue $15.03 billion; non-COVID revenue +18% operationally; guidance midpoint raised by $500 million to $60.5–62.5 billion; $2.5 billion of additional 2027–2029 cost savings; Innovent Biologics deal closed in July. AbbVie: Q2 revenue +10.2% to $16.99 billion; Skyrizi $5.5 billion (+24%) and Rinvoq $2.5 billion (+23.7%); guidance raised to ~$67.6 billion; planned Apogee Therapeutics acquisition. Novartis: Q2 net sales +1% at constant currencies with full-year guidance reaffirmed ( Q2 report ); Kisqali +43% cc, Scemblix +89% cc. Novo Nordisk: Q2 adjusted sales +7% CER to DKK 78.5 billion; 2026 guidance raised a second time to 0% to -6% adjusted growth; oral Wegovy passed 5 million cumulative U.S. prescriptions. GSK: Q2 core operating profit +7%. Pharma Revenue vs. Total Company Revenue Why the “largest” company depends on how you count. Johnson & Johnson’s $94.2 billion includes MedTech ($33.8 billion in 2025), while Eli Lilly, Merck and AbbVie are almost entirely drug businesses. On a drugs-only basis the picture is tighter: J&J’s Innovative Medicine segment generated $16.38 billion in Q2 2026 and $16.76 billion in Q3, versus $22.97 billion for Lilly in Q2. Sinopharm’s ~$80 billion is mostly distribution revenue, and Roche includes a Diagnostics division (CHF 10.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026). This is why we show total reported revenue in the ranking and flag mixed business models in the notes. Largest Pharma Companies by Revenue: Company-by-Company Breakdown 1. Johnson & Johnson — $94.2 Billion J&J grew 2025 sales about 6% to $94.2 billion from $88.8 billion, per its Q4 and full-year 2025 results . Oncology grew 22% in Innovative Medicine, with Darzalex above $14.3 billion and Carvykti nearly doubling to $1.9 billion, while Stelara biosimilar erosion cut Immunology revenue by roughly $4.3 billion. MedTech contributed $33.8 billion. Growth also came from Spravato, Xarelto and the 2025 acquisition of Intra-Cellular Therapies, whose schizophrenia and bipolar drug Caplyta earned a major-depressive-disorder add-on label and about $700 million in 2025 revenue. The 2023 Kenvue consumer-health spin-off has not slowed momentum. 2026: After the Q3 report, J&J guides to $101.0–101.4 billion in reported sales, crossing $100 billion for the first time (see the [Q3 update](#q3)). Headwinds include generic and biosimilar erosion for Opsumit and Simponi, which together had more than $2.8 billion in U.S. sales in 2025 ( FiercePharma ), and the talc litigation charge booked in Q3. Market capitalization: ~$620B ( TradingView , early Aug 2026; affiliate link). 2. Sinopharm Group — ~$80.0 Billion (RMB 575.2 Billion) Sinopharm Group, a core subsidiary of China National Pharmaceutical Group and listed in Hong Kong, reported 2025 revenue of RMB 575.2 billion (about $80 billion). It is China’s largest wholesaler and retailer of drugs and medical devices, serving more than 700,000 institutional customers; pharmaceutical distribution is over 70% of revenue, with devices and retail pharmacy (including Guoda Drugstore) making up the rest. Important distinction: Sinopharm is a distributor, the Chinese equivalent of McKesson or Cardinal Health, not an R&D-driven drug maker like the other 19 companies here. Thin distribution margins explain why a company with ~$80 billion in sales has a market cap of only ~$8.3 billion, smaller than Regeneron’s (~$82 billion on $14.3 billion in revenue). Treat revenue rankings that include distributors separately from manufacturer rankings. Related: In June 2026 China approved satri-cel (CT041), the first CAR-T therapy approved for a solid tumor . 3. Roche — ~$70 Billion (CHF 61.5 Billion) Roche’s 2025 group sales were CHF 61.5 billion, up 7% at constant exchange rates (2% in francs, reflecting a strong franc). Pharmaceuticals grew 9% CER to CHF 47.7 billion, led by five growth drivers (Phesgo, Xolair, Ocrevus, Hemlibra, Vabysmo) worth CHF 21.4 billion together; Xolair rose 32% on a new food-allergy indication. Roche aims to be a top-three global obesity company by 2030 and reported competitive Phase 2 data for CT-388 in early 2026. 2026: First-half sales grew 6% CER, with U.S. Vabysmo sales weaker than analysts expected. Nine-month sales reached CHF 46.5 billion (+6% CER, +1% CHF) and Q3 accelerated to +7% CER; the mid-single-digit growth outlook was confirmed on October 22 ( release ). Roche is preparing a U.S. launch of breast-cancer drug giredestrant by year-end. 4. Eli Lilly and Company — $65.2 Billion Lilly had the industry’s standout year: revenue up 45% to $65.2 billion, per its Q4 2025 release . Mounjaro nearly doubled to $23.0 billion and Zepbound rose 175% to $13.5 billion, together $36.5 billion, more than the annual revenue of Gilead or Amgen. Tirzepatide became the world’s best-selling drug franchise, overtaking Merck’s Keytruda. Lilly was the first drugmaker to reach a $1 trillion valuation in November 2025. Its oral GLP-1 orforglipron (Foundayo) won FDA approval in April 2026, after an HSBC downgrade in March flagged pricing pressure and launch risk. Q2 2026 (reported Aug 5): revenue +47.7% to $22.97 billion, adjusted EPS $8.38 (about 27% above consensus) and full-year guidance raised to $85–87 billion from the earlier $80–83 billion range. Pricing is still a drag: management has cited low- to mid-teens price erosion, a White House drug-pricing deal and Chinese Mounjaro coverage as variables. Q3 results are due in late October. Market capitalization: ~$1.1T ( TradingView , early Aug 2026; affiliate link). Related: GLP-1 Investing Hub | GLP-1 2.0: Next-Generation Obesity Drugs | GLP-1 Studies Explained | Eli Lilly vs. Novo Nordisk 5. Merck & Co. (MSD outside the U.S. and Canada) — $65.0 Billion Merck’s 2025 worldwide sales were $65.0 billion, up 1% ( results ). Keytruda grew 7% to $31.7 billion, about 49% of revenue, with U.S. patent protection expected to end around December 2028. Gardasil fell 39% to $5.2 billion on weak China and Japan demand, and the CDC’s move to a single-dose HPV schedule could cost $315–630 million in 2026, per a Jefferies estimate . Diversification is the strategy: Winrevair reached $1.4 billion and Capvaxive $759 million in 2025, and Merck has spent heavily on acquisitions (Verona for about $10 billion, Cidara for $9.2 billion and Terns for roughly $6.7–6.8 billion). Management still targets about $70 billion in revenue by the middle of the next decade. 2026: Q2 revenue rose 5% to $16.6 billion and guidance was raised to $66.3–67.3 billion (from $65.5–67.0 billion). Merck holds an investor event at ESMO on October 29. Related: Moderna–Merck Cancer Vaccine Phase 3 Results | 25 Landmark KEYNOTE Trials 6. AbbVie — $61.2 Billion AbbVie’s 2025 net revenue rose 8.6% to $61.2 billion, completing the post-Humira transition.
